_comment: Print-on-demand product config. One entry per deck. The print page reads this to show a 'Buy a printed deck' button. To go live: create the product at your vendor, paste its public product/checkout URL into product_url (add any affiliate tag there), and set status to 'live'. back_image is optional — when set, the print page offers a deck-back option.

default_vendor.name: The Game Crafter
default_vendor.note: You are the seller; you earn margin per sale (better than a typical affiliate cut). Affiliate-tagged URLs also work — just paste them into product_url.

rights.work: PD (Pamela Colman Smith and A. E. Waite, 1909; US PD, UK/EU PD since 2022)
rights.scan_source: The Commons 'RWS Tarot' set (Commons credit: muzendo.jp). Which printing it shows is not recorded.
rights.sale_gate: Before a sale: confirm the scans show a 1909–1910 printing, not a U.S. Games-era recolour. RIDER-WAITE-SMITH is a registered U.S. Games trademark for printed tarot cards (Reg. No. 7232194): never in a product title, on the box, or on the card faces.

rights.scan_source: All 147 images are the Commons set 'Minchiate card deck - Florence - 1860-1890', whose Commons credit is Gallica, ark:/12148/btv1b105161123 (BnF). The Commons page tags them public domain; that is a claim about the work, not a grant from the BnF.
rights.sale_gate: NOT saleable as-is. Gallica allows free non-commercial reuse with the credit 'Source gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France'; commercial reuse needs a BnF licence (playing cards: a negotiated percentage of sales, https://www.bnf.fr/en/order-reproduction-commercial-use). A private proof copy is fine. Get the licence, or re-source from a licence-free scan, before setting status=live.

tarot-de-marseille-conver.note: All 78 print-ready via metadata.print.tgc_url (border_fit 900x1500 R2 masters). COMPOSITE deck: 24 cards are Conver 1760, 54 are a Lequart c.1890 Marseille re-edition — see rights.

rights.work: PD (Conver 1760 pattern; the 54 pips/courts are a Lequart, Paris, c.1890 lithographic re-edition of the same pattern — also PD)
rights.scan_source: Two Wikimedia Commons sets, verified 2026-09-08 via the Commons API (extmetadata). (a) 24 cards — 22 trumps + Ace of Swords + Ace of Batons — 'LE MAT Nicolas Conver Tarot 1760.jpg' etc., uploaded 2025-08-09 by user 'Tarot World Project', credit 'Own work', licence CC BY-SA 4.0, description: 'Card ... from the Nicolas Convert Tarot deck (1760), reprint by Reality Publishing (2020)' — i.e. photographs of a 2020 commercial reprint, not an institutional scan of the 1760 object. (b) 54 cards — all other pips/courts, '4P_Tarot.png' etc., uploaded 2019-09-08 by user 'Antoni18072016', credit = Gallica https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b10539498w (BnF Estampes, BOITE FOL-KH-383, '[Jeu de tarot à enseignes italiennes], Édition Lequart avant 1890, lithographie en couleur, 11,9 x 6,3 cm', Collection Paul Marteau). Gallica IIIF manifest license = https://gallica.bnf.fr/html/und/conditions-dutilisation-des-contenus-de-gallica.
rights.sale_gate: NOT saleable as-is. 54/78 faces are Gallica/BnF scans: Gallica terms allow non-commercial reuse only; commercial use (a printed deck for sale) needs a BnF licence — for playing cards BnF charges a negotiated percentage of sales, no per-image fee (see memory: Tarot as Myth 1.1). A private proof copy is fine. The 24 Tarot World Project faces are CC BY-SA 4.0: commercial use is allowed but the colophon/box MUST credit 'Tarot World Project (Wikimedia Commons), CC BY-SA 4.0' and the deck stays share-alike; residual risk that Reality Publishing claims restoration rights in its 2020 reprint (unverified). Either obtain the BnF licence, or re-source the 54 minors from a licence-free scan, before setting status=live. Also: the title 'Conver 1760' is only accurate for 24 cards — the box/colophon say so.
